original_value: Compared to sequential learning models, graph-based neural networks exhibit some excellent properties, such as ability capturing global information. In this paper, we investigate graph-based neural networks for text classification problem. A new framework TensorGCN (tensor graph convolutional networks), is presented for this task. A text graph tensor is firstly constructed to describe semantic, syntactic, and sequential contextual information. Then, two kinds of propagation learning perform on the text graph tensor. The first is intra-graph propagation used for aggregating information from neighborhood nodes in a single graph. The second is inter-graph propagation used for harmonizing heterogeneous information between graphs. Extensive experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets, and the results illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework. Our proposed TensorGCN presents an effective way to harmonize and integrate heterogeneous information from different kinds of graphs.

result.paraphrase: Compared with sequential learning models, graph-based neural networks have notable advantages, including the ability to capture global information. In this paper, we study graph-based neural networks for text classification and present a new framework, TensorGCN (tensor graph convolutional networks), for this task. First, a text graph tensor is constructed to represent semantic, syntactic, and sequential contextual information. Then two forms of propagation learning are applied to the text graph tensor. The first, intra-graph propagation, aggregates information from neighboring nodes within a single graph. The second, inter-graph propagation, reconciles heterogeneous information across graphs. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed framework. TensorGCN offers an effective approach for harmonizing and integrating heterogeneous information from different graph types.
